messages.subject: Re: featureCounts does not accept negative coordinates
messages.subject_clean: featureCounts does not accept negative coordinates
messages.body_plain:
Since BAM and SAM specification doesn't allow negative or zero coordinates of the mapping locations, it is meaningless to have negative coordinates in the GTF files. Even the GTF file contains exons starting at negative coordinates, no reads can be mapped to the "negative parts" of the exons by any aligner -- unless they don't use SAM or BAM format.

Why there are negative coordinates for the exons on circular chromosomes? For example, if an exon is annotated as starting at -1000 and ending at 500, does it mean that the exon starts at the 1000th base before the "reference zero point" and ends at the 500th base after the "reference zero point"? If so, we can add a new function in featureCounts to allow exons starts at negative coordinates, if the chromosome length is known: if we see an exon start at -1000 and ends at 500, featureCounts can split it into two exons: the first exon is from (chro_length - 1000) to chro_length, and the other exon is from 1 to 500. Would this solve the problem?

messages.subject: Re: Subread not able to perform alignment ?
messages.subject_clean: Subread not able to perform alignment ?
messages.body_plain:
I'm not sure what is the step of running where Subread got stuck since you're using the very basic setting for running Subread-align.

Would it be possible to start subread-align using gdb? Like

$ gdb ./subread-align

> set args -T 5  -i  /data/subread-1.6.2-Linux-x86_64/index/hg38  -r /data/Chi-son/lastl/SRR_R1.fastq -R /data/Chi-son/lastl/SRR_R2.fastq -t 1 -o /data/subread-1.6.2-Linux-x86_64/SRR.subread1.sam

> run

When it got stuck, just press Ctrl+C to stop it, and use  the where command to see the current location of the source code.

By the way, I noticed that your output file is a SAM file. You should use the "--SAMoutput" option to actually generate a SAM-formated output, or the file format will still be BAM although the file name suffix is ".sam".
